title: Hollow Street
hook: The night bus driver had one rule: if we ever stop at Hollow Street, keep your eyes down and don't let anything sit next to you.
lines: I ride the last bus home every night, all the way to the end of the line.
The driver, an old man named Ray, gave me one rule on my first ride.
If this bus ever stops at Hollow Street... keep your eyes down. And don't let anything sit next to you.
There is no Hollow Street. Not on any map.
For a whole year, we never stopped there. Just rain, empty seats, and Ray humming to the radio.
Then, one night, the bus slowed down... between two black fields.
The doors hissed open. Ray didn't say a word.
I stared at my shoes. Slow, wet footsteps came up the steps... and down the aisle.
I put my bag on the empty seat. And I didn't breathe.
After a long time, the footsteps turned... and went back to the front.
As we pulled away, I saw Ray through the back window... standing in the rain at Hollow Street, waving goodbye.
The driver never turned around. He just said, in Ray's voice...
Don't worry. I know where you live.
